verdict.reasoning: Patient reports “problems with my hearing, I can't really hear very well” and “my face has been feeling a bit numb… just one side, just on my left side” and states duration “been a few weeks now… been about three weeks or something.”

Location: “again it's the left side, it's kind of like around my left ear, and kind of, along here. So like, my jawline's just all feeling a bit numb round here.” Chronicity: when asked if numbness is present now, patient says “yeah. It kind of, kind of, there quite often, so, all the time.”

Intermittent tinnitus: “I think, occasionally noticed a, ringing in my ear.” Side is implied as same symptomatic (left) side. No otorrhea: “do you have any discharge coming from that ear at all? Patient: No, nothing, nothing coming out.” No otalgia: “Any pain in the ear, or from the ear? Patient: Uh, no, don't think so.”

Patient states, “because of all the kind of, these symptoms I've been getting, especially sometimes when I get a ringing, I can feel a bit dizzy” and later repeats “when I get that I can sometimes feel a bit dizzy,” indicating dizziness occasionally accompanies the ringing.

No limb symptoms: “have you had any weakness or numbness, down the, in the rest of the body at all? Patient: No, no, no, no, nothing like that.” No dysphagia: “Have you had any difficulty swallowing? Patient: No.” No dysarthria: “have you had any difficulty speaking? Patient: No, no.” No visual changes: “Have you noticed any problems with your vision, at all? Patient: No, that's all good.”
Fever queried directly: “have you had any fever at all? Patient: No, nothing like that.”
Patient history: “I've got kind of, been told I have polyps in my nose in the past.”
Remote labyrinthitis: “Other than that I think they said, ages ago, I had something called, can't quite remember but, labyrinthitis, something like that, but again, nothing, nothing ongoing.”
Nasal spray PRN, name unknown: “I only take the, spray for my nose when I need it” and when asked the name, “Do you remember the name of the spray, at all? Patient: Unfortunately I don't, sorry.”
Rennies PRN: “I take a Rennie's if I need to” and later “sometimes take like Rennies, but I just get that from the chemist.”
Allergy: “Do you have any , any allergies to any medication? Patient: Uh, no just Latex. Doctor: Latex, OK.”
Family history: “My brother had, Neurofibromatosis, I think it is. Um, other than that everyone else is OK.”

Occupation and reduced training: “Yeah, so I'm a, I'm a jockey” and “because of all the kind of, these symptoms I've been getting… I've just had to do far less training. So, kind of beginning to, yeah, impacting work, um, a little bit now.”

Patient first says “Yeah, yeah.” to “do you live alone?” but immediately corrects: “Um, I, uh, live with my partner.” Thus the patient does not live alone and does live with a partner. “Do you have any pets at all at home? Patient: No, no pets.” The pet status is correct, but the claim that the patient lives with a partner without ambiguity conflicts with the initial “Yeah, yeah” to living alone; transcript is inconsistent, so this statement is not cleanly supported.

Clinician impression: “what you're describing might be something called Bell's Palsy” and “I would like you to be assessed in a clinic today… so that we can do a… neurological examination… Have a look inside the ear.” This indicates Bell’s palsy is considered and in-person neurological and ear exam is required.

Health anxiety: patient says looking online made them “panic” and “get a bit, frantic,” worried “hopefully nothing so serious I will die from it.” Reassurance: doctor responds “from what you've told me, this doesn't seem to be… anything that you're gonna die from… preliminarily I can, I can reassure you.”
Plan for same-day face-to-face: “I would like you to be assessed in a clinic today” and later “please make sure the appointment gets done today.”

Neurological and ear exam: “we can do a… neurological examination just to make sure there's nothing else going on… Have a look, have a look inside the ear, see if there's any, anything to see within the ear.” Cranial nerves are a standard component of a neurological exam and are reasonably implied.

Bell’s palsy to be discussed after exam: “what you're describing might be something called Bell's Palsy… We can go into that, explaining what that is, if… that's confirmed on, on physical examination.”

Booking instructions: “I'm gonna send a message to our admin team… to book you in for a face-to-face appointment in one of our clinics… within Central London. OK, and then you can ring the, the support team number, I'll leave that number in your notes. And you can ring them after five minutes, and then they'll slot you in to a place that's convenient for you.”

Reassurance and emphasis on exam: “this doesn't seem to be… anything that you're gonna die from… preliminarily I can, I can reassure you. However… in order to definitively reassure you, I, I think you need a physical examination today… please make sure the appointment gets done today.”
